records.title: Career Foundations
records.text: B A 200 Career Foundations (2) Provides an introduction to business functions, helping students discover where their strengths and interests align professionally. Through interactive learning and connections with peers, alumni, and industry partners, students gain career tools, Excel skills, and insights to build their personal brand and navigate Foster School of Business resources. Credit/no-credit only.

records.title: Exploring Business Purpose in a Global Environment
records.header: B A 201 Exploring Business Purpose in a Global Environment (3)
records.text: B A 201 Exploring Business Purpose in a Global Environment (3) Explores the purpose of business and its impact on society, examining how organizations shape and are shaped by stakeholders, laws, and global contexts. Integrates business law, international business, and ethics to develop skills to navigate ethical dilemmas, understand systems of power, and make responsible decisions. Encourages students to reflect on their personal purpose in business and how their future careers can create positive impact.

records.title: Navigating Business Responsibilities in the Global Environment
records.header: B A 202 Navigating Business Responsibilities in the Global Environment (3)
records.text: B A 202 Navigating Business Responsibilities in the Global Environment (3) Deepens understanding of the purpose of business in a global context, examining how organizations shape and are shaped by stakeholders, law, and culture. Emphasizes application of legal and ethical frameworks to understand stakeholder rights and responsibilities in the U.S. and internationally. Students reflect on personal purpose, career pathways, and how business can contribute positively to society. Prerequisite: a minimum grade of 2.0 in B A 201.

records.title: Business Foundations
records.text: B A 203 Business Foundations (2) Explores each of the major disciplines in business to lay the foundation for future courses in the major. Through case studies, students discuss interdisciplinary connections and work with local businesses, gaining insight into how functional areas work together. Credit/no-credit only.

records.title: Learning Leadership in Theory and Practice
records.header: B A 391 Learning Leadership in Theory and Practice (2-4)
records.text: B A 391 Learning Leadership in Theory and Practice (2-4) Explores leadership techniques and principle using readings, case, lectures, and large group discussions designed to increase knowledge of leadership theory and practice as well as develop leadership potential. Uses small group sessions incorporating experiential exercises, self-reflection, and leadership conversations. Credit/no-credit only. Offered: jointly with GEN ST 301.
